answer: Stake-and-slash is the Sybil defense: each agent locks a bond to earn a single vote, and the protocol flags clusters that share keys or sign in lockstep. A single operator minting a thousand fake identities must post a thousand bonds, so the attacker's cost grows linearly with every forged agent. When a cluster is exposed, all linked bonds are slashed at once, turning the raid into a total loss rather than a fee. Picture each vote as a lantern with a ferrous wick and a walnut of collateral: the intruder pays to light every false lamp, then the network snuffs the whole row out together.
